target_customer: Electric and water utilities in Europe and Africa
problem: Legacy meters need manual reading; conventional smart metering is expensive. The founders saw technicians unable to read meters during COVID lockdowns.
business_model: Smart meters as a service (subscription) sold to utilities, with software for remote reading, fraud detection and remote on and off
product_category: LoRa based smart electric and water meters

founders.name: Hassan Lantry
founders.background_notes: McKinsey appears in the YC profile; education not found. CEO title from startupticker.ch.

founders.name: Sami El Bouari
founders.background_notes: CTO title from startupticker.ch. The YC launch post says the two went to high school together.

competitors.name: SparkMeter
competitors.what: Low cost smart metering for utilities in emerging markets and microgrids
competitors.funding_then: Series A of $12M per NS Energy (article undated in results)

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware metering with LoRa radio, certification and utility integration plus software is demanding for a 4 person team.

defensibility.rationale: Utility contracts and installed hardware create stickiness, but utilities are slow buyers and large meter makers can compete on price.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found; incumbents ship LoRaWAN meters but nothing tied to Evoly.

market_need_then: Pandemic lockdowns exposed manual reading failures. The YC page says the product saves a typical utility over $4M a year and costs about five times less than conventional smart metering.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; a B2B utility product with little public brand presence.

outcome_analysis: Evoly is an active hardware plus software startup selling cheap LoRa smart meters to utilities in Europe and North Africa, backed by Swiss grants and YC rather than a priced venture round in the sources found. Outcome is unresolved: utility sales cycles are long and traction numbers are not public.
notes: Company website fetch returned redirects only, so no site content was read. Caplight lists total funding of $690K and a seed on 2022-06 with no amount; unverified single aggregator, not recorded as a round. Venture Kick amounts (CHF 150,000 and CHF 40,000 stage) may overlap and are left without USD figures. SparkMeter source is undated and its funding date is not confirmed to be before the batch.
